title: Files and directories with NIO.2: `Path`, `Files` and walking a tree

videos.script: Lesson 19 read files through streams wrapped around streams. Most code today goes through a shorter door, the package java dot nio dot file. {{path}} It starts with Path, which is a name and nothing more. Building one, joining two, tidying a path full of dots: none of it touches the disk. {{files}} Then Files, a class of static methods that does touch it. Write a file in one line, read it back in one line, or read it as a stream of lines, lazily, with the filters and sums of lessons 6 to 9. {{walk}} Then a whole tree: list a folder, walk every level below it, find the large files, and delete the lot in the right order. {{fail}} And last, what goes wrong. Each refusal has its own exception, and a file name that arrives from outside has to be kept inside the folder it was meant for.
